# #241 — AgentOutcome carries the agent's FINAL message as a distinct field

Waffles' Defect-3 ruling (fleet run 2), pulled forward on Tom's press
2026-08-14 23:46Z ("It's not good enough to have things that are working
coming up as failed"). Ratified by Waffles 23:47Z: "the final message as its
own field on AgentOutcome, harness-side in every adapter, and the judge reads
THAT field."

## The defect this kills

The ACP harness accumulates EVERY completed agent answer of a session into
`AgentOutcome.text` (joined). A workflow that routes on an exact reply token
(fleet_dev's judge: reply exactly `fleet-judge-pass`) can never match when the
agent narrates before its verdict — the token is buried in the accumulation.
Fleet run 2's judge PASSED both duties and said the exact token as its last
message, yet the run recorded WorkflowFailed. A working delivery wore a failed
badge in the operator's console. Direction of error is false-alarm, never
false-accept — keep that property.

## The contract change

`AgentOutcome` (crates/aion-core/src/agent_outcome.rs) gains a mandatory
fourth field:

```
pub struct AgentOutcome {
    pub text: String,          // unchanged: the run's whole output (accumulated)
    pub final_message: String, // NEW: the agent's LAST completed message, alone
    pub stop_reason: String,   // unchanged
    pub session_id: String,    // unchanged
}
```

This is a REPLACEMENT, not an addition beside (house law: no backwards
compatibility, no compat shims). Follow the #205 precedent exactly:

- The wire shape is exactly the four snake_case keys.
- A three-field payload NO LONGER DECODES (pin with a test, as
  `a_two_field_payload_no_longer_decodes` pins the previous widening —
  update/extend that test family).
- A three-field AWL declaration NO LONGER CHECKS (checker change below).
- `AgentOutcome::new` takes the final message as a parameter — no defaulting,
  no `Option`, no builder that lets a harness forget it.

Semantics of `final_message`:

- The LAST completed agent ANSWER message of the run, exactly as the agent
  said it. Not reasoning, not tool output, not user turns.
- Empty is honest when the agent produced no answer text at all (tool-only
  turn): both `text` and `final_message` are `""` then. NO refusal on empty
  final_message (unlike session_id — an agent that said nothing said nothing).
- When the run produced exactly one answer message, `final_message == text`.
  That equality is the honest degenerate case, not a bug.

## Sites (R1..R7)

R1 — **aion-core** `agent_outcome.rs`: the field, the doc comments (state the
semantics above, including WHY the field exists — the fleet-judge false-flag),
`new()` signature, tests: 4-key wire shape pinned as JSON; 3-field payload
refused at decode; round-trip; empty final_message survives.

R2 — **aion-integration-acp**: `MessageAccumulator`
(src/messages.rs) additionally tracks the text of the LAST completed agent
ANSWER (reasoning/user streams never touch it; `finish()` must fold a
still-open answer in, same as `completed_text` does). `PromptOutcome`
(src/outcome.rs) carries it alongside `text`; `outcome_into_payload` feeds it
to `AgentOutcome::new`. Tests: a turn with three answer messages → `text` is
all three joined, `final_message` is the third alone (THIS is the defect's
pin — it must fail on the old accumulate-only behavior); single-message turn
→ equal; tool-only turn → both empty; thought-chunks never contaminate
final_message.

R3 — **aion-integration-norn** (src/translate.rs:242): norn's envelope
`output` IS the final value by norn's own protocol (DRIVEN-PROTOCOL.md stop
envelope), so `final_message` = the same string as `text`. Say so in a doc
comment citing the protocol — the duplication is honest, not lazy.

R4 — **aion-integration-cli** (src/session.rs:300 + src/mock.rs:150): same —
the CLI harness's `final_line` is already the final message; both fields get
it. Doc comment states it.

R5 — **aion-awl checker** (src/checker/agents.rs): the structural demand
becomes exactly FOUR fields (`final_message: String` joins; len == 4). Update
the error message at ~:60 to name all four. `String?` stays refused for the
new field (always present on the wire). Tests: 4-field record checks; 3-field
record refuses naming the missing field; the fixture corpus.

R6 — **the document sweep**: every AWL document in this repo that declares
the agent record must move to the 4-field shape or the corpus gate
(#181's derived gate) goes red — that gate red is your acceptance signal
running green AFTER the sweep. Sweep by the claim's vocabulary (`session_id`
/ `stop_reason` in .awl files and embedded resources), not by a directory
guess: workflows/, the embedded assistant/awl resources in the server crate,
guide examples (aion-awl guide corpus — the guide gates must stay green),
docs/ examples, templates scaffolded by `aion new` if they declare the
record. List EVERY file you touched and every file you checked-and-left in
the report.

R7 — **docs + generated surfaces**: AgentOutcome derives `ts_rs::TS` — check
whether generated TS types are committed (search for the generated
AgentOutcome text) and regenerate if so. Sweep sdks/python, sdks/typescript,
conformance/, and any CLIENT-CONTRACT / API docs for the 3-field shape by
vocabulary (the #211 lesson: the footprint reached sdks/ when the marker said
it didn't). Update prose docs that state the record shape
(AWL-WORKER-DOCUMENTS.md, integration READMEs, DECLARED-COMMANDS.md if it
names the record).

## Out of scope (disclosed non-goals — do NOT take them)

- fleet_dev.awl v3 (judge reads final_message + stdout-token oracle grammar)
  — the dispatcher authors that separately on top of your landing.
- Any deploy, restart, or swap of serving processes (HARD WALL — fleets are
  flying; landed is not running).
- The seated documents under ~/.aion (not in this repo; the dispatcher
  handles reseating at the cut).

## Laws (house, non-negotiable)

- Work ONLY in this worktree (branch 241-final-message). Commit as you go.
  Never push. Never touch ~/.aion, .manifold*, any live process, or files
  outside this worktree.
- No `#[allow]`, `#[expect]`, `#[ignore]`, `_var` renames, `#[cfg(any())]`.
  Clippy fires → fix the code.
- No `.unwrap()`/`.expect()` in library code. Every file ≤500 LOC or split.
- Write the defect's pin (R2's three-message test) FIRST, run it against the
  pre-change accumulator to see it red, and commit it failing with the red
  output quoted in the commit message. Then build until green.
- Gates before you call it done, output to FILES under
  gate-logs/241-final-message/ in the WORKTREE (create it):
  `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` AND
  `cargo clippy -p aion-core -p aion-integration-acp -p aion-integration-norn
  -p aion-integration-cli -p aion-awl --all-targets -- -D warnings` (both
  resolutions are required — feature resolution differs), `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo test --workspace > gate-logs/241-final-message/battery.log 2>&1`
  (never pipe through head/tail — write the file, read the tail after).
  Record the box load beside any red — builders are contending on this box
  and a starvation-shaped red on a loaded box is attributed, not accepted.

## Report (your reply, verbatim demands)

File-by-file: what changed and why. The red-then-green evidence for the R2
pin (commit ids, the quoted red). Every file the R6/R7 sweeps touched AND
every file checked-and-left with why. Every permitted choice made. Every
disclosed non-goal left. Gate exit codes with log paths.

Work from the current repository state. Return only the value required
by the supplied output schema. Do not claim completion or verification
without direct evidence.

1	//! The streamed-message accumulator: turns ACP's per-chunk `session/update` streams into a
2	//! transcript that is both live and durable, and into the run's final text.
3	//!
4	//! # The problem this module exists to solve
5	//!
6	//! ACP streams content as `*_chunk` updates and **never sends a finalised message**. Two
7	//! consequences follow, and both have to be handled here or information is lost:
8	//!
9	//! 1. **Persisting every chunk is the delta-flood defect.** One frame per token, each written
10	//!    durably, rewrites the finished message thousands of times over. So a chunk's live event is
11	//!    *ephemeral* — forwarded to the live channel, never persisted.
12	//! 2. **But then nothing durable would carry the text at all.** So the accumulator buffers each
13	//!    message and, at its boundary, emits ONE durable [`ActivityEventKind::Message`] carrying the
14	//!    whole text. The boundary is a genuinely new `messageId` (see [`MessageAccumulator::finish`]
15	//!    for the other boundary: the end of the turn).
16	//!
17	//! # Three independent streams, accumulated the same way
18	//!
19	//! ACP has three chunk streams, and every one of them is a `ContentChunk` — the protocol makes no
20	//! promise about how many chunks any of them arrives in, so all three are accumulated:
21	//!
22	//! | stream | live event | durable event | in the run's result? |
23	//! |---|---|---|---|
24	//! | `agent_message_chunk` | ephemeral [`ActivityEventKind::Delta`] | `Message { role: Assistant }` | **yes** |
25	//! | `agent_thought_chunk` | ephemeral `Progress::Note` | `Message { role: Assistant }` | no |
26	//! | `user_message_chunk` | none (see below) | `Message { role: User }` | no |
27	//!
28	//! - **Reasoning is durable.** A run whose reasoning existed only on an ephemeral channel would
29	//!   leave nothing behind to audit after the fact, which defeats the point of a durable transcript.
30	//!   [`ActivityEventKind::Message`] is documented as the home for "assistant text/thinking", so
31	//!   that is where accumulated reasoning lands. **Known limitation:** the neutral
32	//!   [`MessageRole`] vocabulary has no reasoning role, so a durable reasoning message and a durable
33	//!   answer message are both `Message { role: Assistant }` and a consumer cannot tell them apart.
34	//!   Inventing a role or a marker would be fabrication; the distinction that IS preserved is the
35	//!   one that matters for correctness — only the `agent_message_chunk` stream contributes to
36	//!   [`MessageAccumulator::completed_text`], so reasoning can never leak into the activity's
37	//!   replay-authoritative result.
38	//! - **A user chunk has no live event.** The neutral [`ActivityEventKind::Delta`] carries no role,
39	//!   so streaming the operator's own words through it would present them downstream as the agent's
40	//!   answer. Nothing is lost: every user chunk's text is in the durable message its boundary emits,
41	//!   and the end of the turn is always a boundary.
42	//!
43	//! The same buffer produces the run's terminal output: ACP's `session/prompt` Response carries only
44	//! a `stopReason`, so the agent's actual answer is the accumulated `agent_message_chunk` text and
45	//! nothing else. See [`MessageAccumulator::completed_text`].
46	//!
47	//! A chunk whose content block is not text (an image, audio, an embedded resource, a resource link)
48	//! is not appendable and is never silently dropped: it becomes a durable
49	//! [`ActivityEventKind::Raw`] carrying the block verbatim.
50	//!
51	//! [`ActivityEventKind::Delta`]: aion_core::ActivityEventKind::Delta
52	//! [`ActivityEventKind::Message`]: aion_core::ActivityEventKind::Message
53	//! [`ActivityEventKind::Raw`]: aion_core::ActivityEventKind::Raw
54	//! [`MessageAccumulator::completed_text`]: crate::messages::MessageAccumulator::completed_text
55	//! [`MessageAccumulator::finish`]: crate::messages::MessageAccumulator::finish
56	//! [`MessageRole`]: aion_core::MessageRole
57	
58	use agent_client_protocol_schema::v1::{ContentBlock, ContentChunk, MessageId};
59	use aion_core::{ActivityEventKind, MessageRole, ProgressDetail};
60	
61	use crate::translate::{EventKind, update_raw};
62	
63	/// The separator inserted between two completed agent messages in [`MessageAccumulator::completed_text`].
64	///
65	/// Two messages are distinct turns of output; concatenating them bare would run the last word of
66	/// one into the first word of the next. A newline is the least surprising join for text an operator
67	/// or a downstream activity will read.
68	const MESSAGE_JOIN: &str = "\n";
69	
70	/// One of ACP's three independent content-chunk streams.
71	///
72	/// Named as an enum rather than three near-copies of the same accumulation logic, so a change to
73	/// the boundary rule cannot apply to one stream and not the others.
74	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
75	enum ChunkStream {
76	    /// `agent_message_chunk` — the agent's answer. The ONLY stream whose text becomes the result.
77	    AgentMessage,
78	    /// `agent_thought_chunk` — the agent's reasoning.
79	    AgentThought,
80	    /// `user_message_chunk` — an operator turn (the prompt, or the agent's echo of it).
81	    User,
82	}
83	
84	impl ChunkStream {
85	    /// The `session/update` variant name this stream's chunks arrive under.
86	    ///
87	    /// Used as the `Raw` source suffix for a chunk whose content block is not text, so the recorded
88	    /// frame names the stream it came from.
89	    const fn variant(self) -> &'static str {
90	        match self {
91	            Self::AgentMessage => "agent_message_chunk",
92	            Self::AgentThought => "agent_thought_chunk",
93	            Self::User => "user_message_chunk",
94	        }
95	    }
96	
97	    /// The neutral role a completed message from this stream is attributed to.
98	    ///
99	    /// Reasoning shares [`MessageRole::Assistant`] with the answer: the agent produced both, and
100	    /// the neutral vocabulary has no reasoning role to distinguish them (see the module docs).
101	    const fn role(self) -> MessageRole {
102	        match self {
103	            Self::AgentMessage | Self::AgentThought => MessageRole::Assistant,
104	            Self::User => MessageRole::User,
105	        }
106	    }
107	
108	    /// Whether this stream's completed text is part of the run's result.
109	    ///
110	    /// Only the agent's answer is. Folding reasoning or an echoed user turn into the result would
111	    /// hand the workflow text the agent never offered as its answer.
112	    const fn feeds_the_result(self) -> bool {
113	        matches!(self, Self::AgentMessage)
114	    }
115	}
116	
117	/// One message being streamed: the `messageId` it is tagged with (ACP allows none) and the text
118	/// accumulated so far.
119	#[derive(Debug)]
120	struct OpenMessage {
121	    /// The chunk `messageId` this message is accumulating under. `None` is a real state, not a
122	    /// missing value: an agent may stream a whole message without tagging it.
123	    id: Option<MessageId>,
124	    /// The text accumulated from every chunk seen for this message, in arrival order.
125	    text: String,
126	}
127	
128	/// Accumulates ACP's streamed content chunks into durable messages and the run's final text.
129	#[derive(Debug, Default)]
130	pub struct MessageAccumulator {
131	    /// The agent answer currently being streamed, if any.
132	    agent_message: Option<OpenMessage>,
133	    /// The agent reasoning block currently being streamed, if any.
134	    agent_thought: Option<OpenMessage>,
135	    /// The user turn currently being streamed, if any.
136	    user: Option<OpenMessage>,
137	    /// Every completed AGENT ANSWER's text, joined by [`MESSAGE_JOIN`] — the run's output so far.
138	    completed: String,
139	}
140	
141	impl MessageAccumulator {
142	    /// An accumulator with nothing streamed yet.
143	    #[must_use]
144	    pub fn new() -> Self {
145	        Self::default()
146	    }
147	
148	    /// The concatenated text of every agent ANSWER completed so far.
149	    ///
150	    /// This is the run's output: ACP's terminal Response carries only a stop reason, so the agent's
151	    /// answer exists nowhere else. Reasoning and user turns are deliberately absent — they are
152	    /// accumulated and recorded, but they are not the answer. Call [`Self::finish`] before reading
153	    /// it at the end of a turn, so the message still open when the Response arrived is included.
154	    #[must_use]
155	    pub fn completed_text(&self) -> &str {
156	        &self.completed
157	    }
158	
159	    /// Absorbs one `agent_message_chunk`, returning the events it produces in emission order.
160	    ///
161	    /// Emits the durable [`ActivityEventKind::Message`] for a message that just ENDED (when this
162	    /// chunk starts a new one) before the ephemeral [`ActivityEventKind::Delta`] for this chunk, so
163	    /// the transcript reads in the order things happened.
164	    pub fn push_agent_chunk(&mut self, chunk: &ContentChunk) -> Vec<EventKind> {
165	        let (mut events, text) = self.absorb(ChunkStream::AgentMessage, chunk);
166	        if let Some(text) = text {
167	            events.push((
168	                ActivityEventKind::Delta {
169	                    message_id: message_id_label(chunk.message_id.as_ref()),
170	                    text_fragment: text.to_owned(),
171	                },
172	                true,
173	            ));
174	        }
175	        events
176	    }
177	
178	    /// Absorbs one `agent_thought_chunk`, returning the events it produces in emission order.
179	    ///
180	    /// The live event is an ephemeral free-form `Progress::Note` rather than a
181	    /// [`ActivityEventKind::Delta`], because a `Delta` is the answer's token stream and a console
182	    /// appending reasoning to it would corrupt the answer on screen. The durable record is the
183	    /// accumulated message the boundary emits.
184	    pub fn push_thought_chunk(&mut self, chunk: &ContentChunk) -> Vec<EventKind> {
185	        let (mut events, text) = self.absorb(ChunkStream::AgentThought, chunk);
186	        if let Some(text) = text {
187	            events.push((
188	                ActivityEventKind::Progress {
189	                    detail: ProgressDetail::Note {
190	                        text: text.to_owned(),
191	                    },
192	                },
193	                true,
194	            ));
195	        }
196	        events
197	    }
198	
199	    /// Absorbs one `user_message_chunk`, returning the events it produces in emission order.
200	    ///
201	    /// There is no live event for a user chunk (see the module docs): the accumulated durable
202	    /// message its boundary emits is the whole record. A single-chunk user turn therefore produces
203	    /// no event until the turn's [`Self::finish`], which is guaranteed to happen.
204	    pub fn push_user_chunk(&mut self, chunk: &ContentChunk) -> Vec<EventKind> {
205	        let (events, _text) = self.absorb(ChunkStream::User, chunk);
206	        events
207	    }
208	
209	    /// Closes every open message, emitting each one's durable [`ActivityEventKind::Message`].
210	    ///
211	    /// Called at the end of the turn, which is a boundary for all three streams. The order is
212	    /// user, reasoning, then answer, so the agent's answer is the last durable message before the
213	    /// terminal `Stop` event — where a reader looking for the run's output expects it.
214	    ///
215	    /// Returns no event for a stream with nothing open or nothing accumulated — an empty message is
216	    /// not a transcript entry. Idempotent, so the caller may finish a turn without tracking what
217	    /// was open.
218	    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> Vec<EventKind> {
219	        let mut events = Vec::new();
220	        for stream in [
221	            ChunkStream::User,
222	            ChunkStream::AgentThought,
223	            ChunkStream::AgentMessage,
224	        ] {
225	            events.extend(self.close(stream));
226	        }
227	        events
228	    }
229	
230	    /// Appends one chunk's text to `stream`'s buffer.
231	    ///
232	    /// Returns the boundary events (the durable message of the PREVIOUS message on this stream, if
233	    /// this chunk started a new one) and the chunk's text — or, for a chunk whose content block is
234	    /// not text, the verbatim `Raw` event recording it and no text.
235	    fn absorb<'chunk>(
236	        &mut self,
237	        stream: ChunkStream,
238	        chunk: &'chunk ContentChunk,
239	    ) -> (Vec<EventKind>, Option<&'chunk str>) {
240	        let Some(text) = block_text(&chunk.content) else {

242	            let source = format!("{}/content", stream.variant());

244	        };
245	        let mut events = Vec::new();
246	        if self.starts_a_new_message(stream, chunk.message_id.as_ref()) {
247	            events.extend(self.close(stream));
248	        }

1	//! The canonical agent-outcome record — the ONE shape every agent harness
2	//! emits as a completed agent activity's result.
3	//!
4	//! Task #181's ruling (docs commit `c223c8c`): the `agent` marker had
5	//! universalized one harness path's shape (`-> String`, "parse it
6	//! downstream"), while the harnesses honestly emitted three different ad-hoc
7	//! JSON shapes. The fix is this record, defined by aion, snake_case and
8	//! AWL-expressible: every harness maps its native terminal outcome onto it at
9	//! the integration boundary, and a workflow's `agent` action declares a record
10	//! of exactly this shape and reads `text` / `stop_reason` / `session_id` as
11	//! fields.
12	//!
13	//! Task #205's ruling widened the record with a third mandatory field,
14	//! `session_id` — see [`AgentOutcome::session_id`] for its semantics. The
15	//! widening is a replacement, not an addition: the wire shape is exactly the
16	//! three keys, a two-field payload no longer decodes, and a two-field AWL
17	//! declaration no longer checks.
18	//!
19	//! # One stop-reason vocabulary, by subtraction
20	//!
21	//! The canonical `stop_reason` strings are the snake_case renderings of the
22	//! existing neutral [`StopKind`] semantic set — no third stop-reason table
23	//! exists anywhere. [`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`] is the single mapping,
24	//! so the transcript channel (which carries `StopKind` itself) and this
25	//! outcome record cannot drift. `StopKind`'s own serialization is untouched:
26	//! the transcript wire is live and is a different channel from the result.
27	//!
28	//! # The record rides inside a [`Payload`]
29	//!
30	//! Nothing about the type-erased result path changes: an activity result is
31	//! still a [`Payload`] of `{content_type, bytes}`. The record is the JSON the
32	//! bytes carry for a completed agent activity.
33	
34	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
35	
36	use crate::activity_event::StopKind;
37	use crate::payload::{ContentType, Payload};
38	
39	impl StopKind {
40	    /// The canonical `snake_case` `stop_reason` string for this stop kind.
41	    ///
42	    /// This is the ONE mapping from the neutral stop vocabulary onto the
43	    /// [`AgentOutcome::stop_reason`] wire strings. The detail payloads of
44	    /// [`StopKind::Error`] and [`StopKind::Other`] deliberately do not reach
45	    /// the canonical string: the canonical vocabulary is closed, and the
46	    /// detail belongs to the transcript channel that carries the full
47	    /// `StopKind`.
48	    #[must_use]
49	    pub fn canonical_stop_reason(&self) -> &'static str {
50	        match self {
51	            Self::EndTurn => "end_turn",
52	            Self::ToolUse => "tool_use",
53	            Self::LimitReached => "limit_reached",
54	            Self::Cancelled => "cancelled",
55	            Self::Error { .. } => "error",
56	            Self::Other { .. } => "other",
57	        }
58	    }
59	}
60	
61	/// The error serializing an [`AgentOutcome`] as its result [`Payload`].
62	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
63	pub enum AgentOutcomeError {
64	    /// The record's mandatory `session_id` is the empty string.
65	    ///
66	    /// A vacant mandatory field is a harness bug, refused here by name at the
67	    /// one funnel every harness serializes through — never shipped as a
68	    /// silently empty handle a workflow would try to resume with.
69	    #[error(
70	        "the agent-outcome record's mandatory `session_id` is empty — every harness fills it \
71	         with the handle of the conversation that produced this outcome, and an empty handle \
72	         names no conversation"
73	    )]
74	    EmptySessionId,
75	    /// The record could not be encoded as JSON — unreachable for three plain
76	    /// strings, but never swallowed.
77	    #[error("the agent-outcome record is not encodable: {0}")]
78	    Encode(#[from] serde_json::Error),
79	}
80	
81	/// The canonical agent-outcome record: what a completed agent activity's
82	/// result payload carries, from every harness.
83	///
84	/// Three fields, all `snake_case`, all mandatory, all AWL-expressible — the
85	/// AWL checker demands an `agent` action's declared return type be a record of
86	/// exactly this shape (`text: String`, `stop_reason: String`,
87	/// `session_id: String`), so a workflow reads `reply.text`,
88	/// `reply.stop_reason`, and `reply.session_id` as ordinary record fields.
89	///
90	/// An empty `text` on a completed run is honest, not a bug: an agent that
91	/// finished its turn having emitted only tool calls said nothing, and the
92	/// harness reports that truth rather than inventing words (the work is on the
93	/// transcript). `stop_reason` is one of the canonical strings produced by
94	/// [`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`]:
95	/// `end_turn | tool_use | limit_reached | cancelled | error | other`.
96	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, ts_rs::TS, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
97	pub struct AgentOutcome {
98	    /// The agent's terminal text — the run's actual output.
99	    pub text: String,
100	    /// The canonical `snake_case` stop reason
101	    /// ([`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`]).
102	    pub stop_reason: String,
103	    /// The handle of the conversation that produced this outcome.
104	    ///
105	    /// A FACT, not a promise: the id names the session the harness actually
106	    /// ran — minted, loaded, or derived by that harness — and says nothing
107	    /// about whether it can be resumed. Resumability is the per-agent question
108	    /// a harness's own handshake answers (for ACP, the `initialize` response's
109	    /// `loadSession` capability), never something this field asserts.
110	    ///
111	    /// The id is meaningful only to the harness that minted it; resume routing
112	    /// pairs the id with the harness identity the workflow record already
113	    /// carries. It is never empty — a harness with a vacant handle is refused
114	    /// at [`AgentOutcome::into_payload`], not shipped.
115	    pub session_id: String,
116	}
117	
118	impl AgentOutcome {
119	    /// Builds the record from the agent's terminal text, the neutral stop
120	    /// kind, and the conversation handle, spelling `stop_reason` through the
121	    /// one canonical mapping.
122	    #[must_use]
123	    pub fn new(text: impl Into<String>, stop: &StopKind, session_id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
124	        Self {
125	            text: text.into(),
126	            stop_reason: stop.canonical_stop_reason().to_owned(),
127	            session_id: session_id.into(),
128	        }
129	    }
130	
131	    /// Serializes the record as the activity's JSON result [`Payload`].
132	    ///
133	    /// # Errors
134	    ///
135	    /// [`AgentOutcomeError::EmptySessionId`] when the mandatory `session_id`
136	    /// is the empty string — the vacancy is refused by name rather than
137	    /// shipped. [`AgentOutcomeError::Encode`] when the record cannot be
138	    /// encoded — unreachable for three plain strings, but never swallowed.
139	    pub fn into_payload(self) -> Result<Payload, AgentOutcomeError> {
140	        if self.session_id.is_empty() {
141	            return Err(AgentOutcomeError::EmptySessionId);
142	        }
143	        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&self)?;
144	        Ok(Payload::new(ContentType::Json, bytes))
145	    }
146	}
147	
148	#[cfg(test)]
149	mod tests {
150	    use serde_json::json;
151	
152	    use super::{AgentOutcome, AgentOutcomeError, StopKind};
153	
154	    type TestResult = Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;
155	
156	    /// The canonical vocabulary is the closed set the ruling names, spelled by
157	    /// exactly one mapping. Enumerated over every variant so a new `StopKind`
158	    /// arm cannot ship without a canonical spelling.
159	    #[test]
160	    fn every_stop_kind_has_its_canonical_snake_case_spelling() {
161	        let cases = [
162	            (StopKind::EndTurn, "end_turn"),
163	            (StopKind::ToolUse, "tool_use"),
164	            (StopKind::LimitReached, "limit_reached"),
165	            (StopKind::Cancelled, "cancelled"),
166	            (
167	                StopKind::Error {
168	                    message: "boom".to_owned(),
169	                },
170	                "error",
171	            ),
172	            (
173	                StopKind::Other {
174	                    reason: "teleported".to_owned(),
175	                },
176	                "other",
177	            ),
178	        ];
179	        for (kind, expected) in cases {
180	            assert_eq!(kind.canonical_stop_reason(), expected);
181	        }
182	    }
183	
184	    /// The wire form is exactly the three `snake_case` keys the AWL record
185	    /// declares — this is the shape every harness emits and every workflow
186	    /// decodes, so it is pinned as JSON, not as a Rust round-trip alone.
187	    #[test]
188	    fn the_record_serializes_as_the_three_snake_case_fields() -> TestResult {
189	        let outcome = AgentOutcome::new("the answer", &StopKind::EndTurn, "sess-7");
190	        assert_eq!(
191	            serde_json::to_value(&outcome)?,
192	            json!({ "text": "the answer", "stop_reason": "end_turn", "session_id": "sess-7" })
193	        );
194	        Ok(())
195	    }
196	
197	    #[test]
198	    fn the_record_round_trips_through_its_payload() -> TestResult {
199	        let outcome = AgentOutcome::new("", &StopKind::EndTurn, "sess-7");
200	        let payload = outcome.clone().into_payload()?;
201	        assert_eq!(payload.content_type(), &super::ContentType::Json);
202	        let decoded: AgentOutcome = serde_json::from_slice(payload.bytes())?;
203	        assert_eq!(decoded, outcome);
204	        assert_eq!(
205	            decoded.text, "",
206	            "an empty text on a completed run is honest and survives the wire"
207	        );
208	        Ok(())
209	    }
210	
211	    /// A vacant mandatory `session_id` is refused by name at the serialization
212	    /// funnel — no harness can ship a silently empty handle.
213	    #[test]
214	    fn an_empty_session_id_is_refused_by_name() -> Result<(), String> {
215	        let error = AgentOutcome::new("the answer", &StopKind::EndTurn, "")
216	            .into_payload()
217	            .err()
218	            .ok_or("an empty session_id must not serialize")?;
219	        assert!(
220	            matches!(error, AgentOutcomeError::EmptySessionId),
221	            "the refusal is the named vacancy, got {error:?}"
222	        );
223	        assert!(
224	            error.to_string().contains("session_id"),
225	            "the refusal names the field: {error}"
226	        );
227	        Ok(())
228	    }
229	
230	    /// A two-field payload — the pre-#205 wire shape — no longer decodes: the
231	    /// widening replaced the record rather than adding beside it, so a stale
232	    /// emitter fails loudly at the decode boundary instead of producing a
233	    /// record with an invented handle.
234	    #[test]
235	    fn a_two_field_payload_no_longer_decodes() {
236	        let stale = json!({ "text": "the answer", "stop_reason": "end_turn" });
237	        let decoded: Result<AgentOutcome, _> = serde_json::from_value(stale);
238	        assert!(
239	            decoded.is_err(),
240	            "the pre-widening shape must be refused, not defaulted"
241	        );
242	    }
243	}

1	//! Interpretation of the terminal `session/prompt` Response as the activity's result.
2	//!
3	//! ACP's prompt Response carries a **stop reason and nothing else**. Two things follow, and both are
4	//! decided here:
5	//!
6	//! 1. **Which stop reasons are a completed run.** Exactly one — `end_turn`. `refusal`, `max_tokens`,
7	//!    and `max_turn_requests` are the agent stopping short of the work, and `cancelled` is a
8	//!    cancellation. Reporting any of them as a completed result would hand a workflow a refused or
9	//!    truncated answer as though it were the real one.
10	//! 2. **Where the answer itself comes from.** Not the Response — it has no output field. The agent's
11	//!    words were streamed as `agent_message_chunk` updates and reassembled by
12	//!    [`crate::messages::MessageAccumulator`], so the accumulated text travels here alongside the
13	//!    Response and becomes the payload's `text`.
14	//!
15	//! # An empty `text` on a completed turn is honest, not a bug
16	//!
17	//! A turn that ends `end_turn` having emitted only tool calls — no `agent_message_chunk` at all —
18	//! yields a SUCCESSFUL result whose `text` is `""`. That is the truth of what happened: the agent
19	//! finished its turn and said nothing, and the work it did is on the transcript as tool events. The
20	//! alternative — failing a turn the agent completed, or substituting the tool output for words the
21	//! agent never spoke — would each report something that did not happen. A caller that requires text
22	//! checks for it; this module will not invent it.
23	
24	use agent_client_protocol_schema::v1::{PromptResponse, SessionId, StopReason};
25	use aion_integrations::jsonrpc::{JsonRpcError, JsonRpcResponse};
26	use aion_integrations::{AgentOutcome, HarnessError, Payload};
27	
28	use crate::protocol;
29	use crate::translate;
30	
31	/// The most of a non-completed turn's partial text that rides in the harness-error message.
32	///
33	/// This bounds an ERROR MESSAGE, not the data: the turn has already failed, and the same text is on
34	/// the transcript in full. It only keeps an enormous partial answer from bloating the persisted
35	/// failure text.
36	///
37	/// **The number is a matched precedent, not a fresh choice.** `aion-integration-norn` bounds the
38	/// same thing — a failed run's partial output riding its terminal error message — with
39	/// `PARTIAL_OUTPUT_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4000` (`aion-integration-norn/src/translate.rs`). Two first-party
40	/// adapters truncating an operator-facing failure message at two different lengths would make the
41	/// same failure read differently depending on which harness ran it, so this adapter takes the
42	/// established value rather than picking its own.
43	const PARTIAL_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES: usize = 4000;
44	
45	/// How the reader pump's turn ended — the ONE signal [`AgentSession::wait_result`] receives.
46	///
47	/// The pump has no error channel of its own, and a dropped sender cannot say WHY it was dropped.
48	/// Naming the three ways a turn can end keeps `wait_result` from asserting a cause that did not
49	/// happen: before this existed, every non-answer was reported as "the agent closed the channel",
50	/// which is false for a reader that hit an I/O failure and false again for a pump that died with an
51	/// answer already in hand.
52	#[derive(Debug)]
53	pub(crate) enum PumpEnd {
54	    /// The id-matched `session/prompt` Response arrived and was interpreted.
55	    ///
56	    /// Boxed because the response frame it carries dwarfs the other two variants, and this enum
57	    /// travels through a `oneshot` channel whose buffer is sized by the largest variant.
58	    Answered(Box<PromptOutcome>),
59	    /// The reader reached end-of-stream — the agent closed its stdout — with the prompt unanswered.
60	    StreamEnded,
61	    /// The reader hit an unrecoverable transport failure with the prompt unanswered.
62	    TransportFailed {
63	        /// The transport error as the reader reported it.
64	        detail: String,

68	/// The terminal outcome of the prompt turn, assembled by the pump and consumed by
69	/// [`AgentSession::wait_result`].
70	///
71	/// The accumulated text travels WITH the response rather than through shared state, so there is no
72	/// window in which `wait_result` could read a buffer the pump had not finished flushing.
73	#[derive(Debug)]
74	pub(crate) struct PromptOutcome {
75	    /// The id-matched `session/prompt` Response, exactly as the agent sent it.
76	    pub(crate) response: JsonRpcResponse,
77	    /// Every agent message completed during the turn, joined — the run's actual output.
78	    pub(crate) text: String,
79	}
80	
81	impl PumpEnd {
82	    /// Interprets a pump end as the activity's [`Payload`], or the honest error it is.
83	    ///
84	    /// `session_id` is the session the turn ran in — minted by `session/new` or restored by
85	    /// `session/load` — and becomes the outcome record's `session_id`: the handle of the
86	    /// conversation that produced this result.
87	    ///
88	    /// # Errors
89	    ///
90	    /// [`HarnessError::Transport`] for a turn that never got an answer, naming which of the two
91	    /// unanswered endings happened; otherwise every error [`outcome_into_payload`] can return.
92	    pub(crate) fn into_payload(self, session_id: &SessionId) -> Result<Payload, HarnessError> {
93	        match self {
94	            Self::Answered(outcome) => outcome_into_payload(*outcome, session_id),
95	            Self::StreamEnded => Err(HarnessError::transport(
96	                "the ACP agent closed its stdout while session/prompt was still outstanding — it \
97	                 exited without answering, so the turn has no terminal result (the agent's own \
98	                 diagnostics are on this process's stderr)",
99	            )),
100	            Self::TransportFailed { detail } => Err(HarnessError::transport(format!(
101	                "the ACP agent's stdout failed while session/prompt was still outstanding, so the \
102	                 turn has no terminal result: {detail}"
103	            ))),
104	        }
105	    }
106	}
107	
108	/// Interprets the terminal outcome as the activity's [`Payload`], or the honest error it is.
109	///
110	/// - **`end_turn`** → the completed run. The payload is the canonical [`AgentOutcome`] record,
111	///   `{"text": <the agent's answer>, "stop_reason": "end_turn", "session_id": <the ACP session>}` —
112	///   ACP's native stop reason mapped through the adapter's existing neutral
113	///   [`translate::stop_kind`] mapping and spelled by the one canonical
114	///   [`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`](aion_integrations::StopKind::canonical_stop_reason)
115	///   vocabulary, and the session the agent itself minted (or reloaded) as the record's
116	///   conversation handle. ACP's Response carries ONLY a stop reason, so the answer itself has to
117	///   come from the accumulated `agent_message_chunk` text; a payload of the stop reason alone
118	///   would hand the workflow an activity result with no result in it.
119	/// - **`refusal`, `max_tokens`, `max_turn_requests`** → [`HarnessError::Harness`] naming the reason.
120	///   None of them is a completed run: the agent stopped short. The partial text rides along,
121	///   labelled and bounded, so a caller's accept-the-partial policy stays reachable.
122	/// - **`cancelled`** → [`HarnessError::Harness`] whose message starts with
123	///   [`protocol::CANCELLED_DETAIL_PREFIX`], so a cancellation is distinguishable from a failure.
124	/// - an **error Response** → [`HarnessError::Harness`]; code `-32000` names the authentication the
125	///   agent is demanding, and `-32800` is reported as a cancellation.
126	/// - a Response with **neither** `result` nor `error` → [`HarnessError::Protocol`]. A broken frame.
127	pub(crate) fn outcome_into_payload(
128	    outcome: PromptOutcome,
129	    session_id: &SessionId,
130	) -> Result<Payload, HarnessError> {
131	    let PromptOutcome { response, text } = outcome;
132	    if let Some(error) = response.error {
133	        return Err(prompt_error(&error, &text));
134	    }
135	    let Some(result) = response.result else {
136	        return Err(HarnessError::protocol(
137	            "the session/prompt response carried neither result nor error",
138	        ));
139	    };
140	    let prompt: PromptResponse = serde_json::from_value(result.clone()).map_err(|source| {
141	        HarnessError::protocol(format!(
142	            "the session/prompt result is not an ACP PromptResponse ({source}): {result}"
143	        ))
144	    })?;
145	    let label = translate::stop_reason_label(prompt.stop_reason);
146	    if !translate::is_success(prompt.stop_reason) {
147	        return Err(non_completion(prompt.stop_reason, label, &text));
148	    }
149	    AgentOutcome::new(
150	        text,
151	        &translate::stop_kind(prompt.stop_reason),
152	        session_id.to_string(),
153	    )
154	    .into_payload()
155	    .map_err(|source| {
156	        HarnessError::protocol(format!("the terminal payload is not encodable: {source}"))
157	    })
158	}
159	
160	/// The honest error for a turn that ended on a stop reason other than `end_turn`.
161	fn non_completion(reason: StopReason, label: &str, text: &str) -> HarnessError {
162	    let mut message = if matches!(reason, StopReason::Cancelled) {
163	        format!("{}: stopReason: {label}", protocol::CANCELLED_DETAIL_PREFIX)
164	    } else {
165	        format!("the prompt turn did not complete: stopReason: {label}")
166	    };
167	    append_partial(&mut message, text);
168	    HarnessError::harness(message)
169	}
170	
171	/// The honest error for a `session/prompt` answered with a JSON-RPC error object.
172	fn prompt_error(error: &JsonRpcError, text: &str) -> HarnessError {
173	    let mut message = if error.code == protocol::auth_required_code() {
174	        format!(
175	            "the agent requires authentication before it will run (code {}): {} — an unattended \
176	             activity cannot complete an interactive `authenticate` flow; configure the agent's \
177	             credentials in the harness environment",
178	            error.code, error.message
179	        )
180	    } else if error.code == protocol::request_cancelled_code() {
181	        format!(
182	            "{}: the agent answered session/prompt with code {} ({}) instead of \
183	             stopReason `cancelled`",
184	            protocol::CANCELLED_DETAIL_PREFIX,
185	            error.code,
186	            error.message
187	        )
188	    } else {
189	        format!(
190	            "session/prompt failed (code {}): {}",
191	            error.code, error.message
192	        )
193	    };
194	    append_partial(&mut message, text);
195	    HarnessError::harness(message)
196	}
197	
198	/// Appends the turn's partial text to a failure message, labelled and bounded.
199	///
200	/// Nothing is appended for an empty partial: fabricating a `partial output:` label for text that does
201	/// not exist would read as though the agent had produced something.
202	fn append_partial(message: &mut String, text: &str) {
203	    if text.is_empty() {
204	        return;
205	    }
206	    message.push_str("; partial output: ");
207	    message.push_str(&bounded_for_message(text));
208	}
209	
210	/// Bounds `rendered` to [`PARTIAL_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES`], appending an explicit truncation marker when
211	/// it was cut. The cut lands on a char boundary so the message stays valid UTF-8.
212	fn bounded_for_message(rendered: &str) -> String {
213	    if rendered.len() <= PARTIAL_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES {
214	        return rendered.to_owned();
215	    }
216	    let mut end = PARTIAL_TEXT_MESSAGE_BYTES;
217	    while !rendered.is_char_boundary(end) {
218	        end -= 1;
219	    }
220	    format!(
221	        "{}… [partial output truncated for this message: {} of {} bytes shown]",
222	        &rendered[..end],
223	        end,
224	        rendered.len()
225	    )
226	}

1	//! The `agent` marker rule.
2	//!
3	//! `agent` on an action declaration says one thing and one thing only: this
4	//! action carries a PROMPT in a `String` parameter and its result is the
5	//! canonical agent-outcome record — a declared record with exactly three
6	//! fields, `text: String` (the agent's terminal reply),
7	//! `stop_reason: String` (the canonical `snake_case` stop reason), and
8	//! `session_id: String` (the handle of the conversation that produced the
9	//! outcome — a fact minted by the harness, not a promise that the session
10	//! can be resumed). That is the
11	//! whole of what an adapter needs in order to hand the call to an agent
12	//! harness instead of executing it as an ordinary activity, and it is the
13	//! shape every harness emits from its `wait_result` boundary (task #181's
14	//! ruling: the record is defined by aion, and every harness maps its native
15	//! outcome onto it — the old `-> String` rule had universalized one harness
16	//! path's shape and flattened the stop reason out of every other's).
17	//!
18	//! Because the shape IS the meaning, the shape has to be enforced here. A
19	//! marker accepted on an action of any shape would be a marker that means
20	//! nothing — a name in the grammar that every reader assumes has force, and
21	//! that nothing gives force to. That is precisely the dormant surface this
22	//! marker exists to remove (the hand-maintained `AGENT_ACTIVITY_TYPES` list in
23	//! a worker binary), so accepting it loosely would re-create the defect one
24	//! layer up instead of closing it.
25	//!
26	//! The author declares the record type themselves, under any name — the
27	//! `RunOutcome` / DECLARED-COMMANDS precedent. The checker demands the
28	//! STRUCTURE, not a blessed name.
29	
30	use crate::ast::{ActionBody, ActionDecl};
31	
32	use super::context::{Callable, Ctx};
33	use super::types::{RecordTy, Ty, TypeTable, resolve};
34	
35	/// Refuse `agent` on an action whose shape cannot carry a prompt and the
36	/// canonical agent-outcome record.
37	///
38	/// Called once per action declaration, with the callable already resolved so
39	/// the parameter and result types are the checker's own types rather than
40	/// unresolved syntax. Nothing is reported when the action does not carry the
41	/// marker.
42	pub(super) fn check(
43	    ctx: &mut Ctx<'_>,
44	    action: &ActionDecl,
45	    callable: &Callable,
46	    bound_directory: Option<&str>,
47	) {
48	    let Some(marker) = action.config.as_ref().and_then(|config| config.agent) else {
49	        return;
50	    };
51	
52	    check_prompt(ctx, action, callable, bound_directory, marker);
53	
54	    if !returns_agent_outcome_record(&callable.returns, &ctx.types) {
55	        ctx.error(
56	            marker,
57	            format!(
58	                "`agent` action `{}` returns `{}` — an agent action returns the canonical \
59	                 agent-outcome record: a declared record with exactly three fields, \
60	                 `text: String`, `stop_reason: String`, and `session_id: String`; every \
61	                 harness emits that record, so declare it (any type name) and read \
62	                 `.text` where the flow needs the reply",
63	                action.name, callable.returns
64	            ),
65	        );
66	    }
67	
68	    // A declared body is executed by the server itself. An `agent` action is
69	    // executed by a harness on a worker. Both at once is two implementations
70	    // of one action, and nothing in the system arbitrates between them.
71	    if let Some(ActionBody::Run { span, .. }) = &action.body {
72	        ctx.error(
73	            *span,
74	            format!(
75	                "action `{}` is marked `agent` and also declares a body — the server runs \
76	                 a declared body itself and never hands it to an agent harness; declare \
77	                 one or the other",
78	                action.name
79	            ),
80	        );
81	    }
82	}
83	
84	/// The prompt rule: exactly one `String` parameter that is not the harness's
85	/// working directory.
86	///
87	/// The prompt is defined by SUBTRACTION rather than by position, because the
88	/// two shapes an agent action can have differ only by the directory: a harness
89	/// naming a literal tree serves actions of one parameter, and a harness taking
90	/// each attempt's tree from the job serves actions that declare that parameter
91	/// too. Counting what remains once the directory is removed states one rule for
92	/// both, instead of an arity that has to be re-derived per shape — and it means
93	/// an action that never declares the bound parameter earns exactly one refusal,
94	/// the harness pass's, rather than a second one here saying the same thing in
95	/// different words.
96	fn check_prompt(
97	    ctx: &mut Ctx<'_>,
98	    action: &ActionDecl,
99	    callable: &Callable,
100	    bound_directory: Option<&str>,
101	    marker: crate::Span,
102	) {
103	    let prompts = callable
104	        .params
105	        .iter()
106	        .filter(|param| Some(param.name.as_str()) != bound_directory)
107	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
108	
109	    // A prompt is one argument. Zero leaves the harness nothing to send; more
110	    // than one leaves it choosing, and a marker whose meaning depends on an
111	    // adapter's choice is not a contract.
112	    if prompts.len() != 1 {
113	        let message = match bound_directory {
114	            None => format!(
115	                "`agent` action `{}` takes {} parameters — an agent action takes exactly \
116	                 one `String`, the prompt; drop `agent` if this is an ordinary action, or \
117	                 carry the extra inputs inside the prompt string",
118	                action.name,
119	                prompts.len()
120	            ),
121	            Some(directory) => format!(
122	                "`agent` action `{}` declares {} parameters besides `{directory}` — its \
123	                 worker's harness takes each attempt's working directory from \
124	                 `{directory}`, so this action takes that `String` and exactly one more, \
125	                 the prompt; carry any further inputs inside the prompt string",
126	                action.name,
127	                prompts.len()
128	            ),
129	        };
130	        ctx.error(marker, message);
131	        return;
132	    }
133	
134	    let prompt = prompts[0];
135	    if !is_string(&prompt.ty) {
136	        let message = match bound_directory {
137	            None => format!(
138	                "`agent` action `{}` takes `{}` — an agent action's one parameter is the \
139	                 `String` prompt handed to the harness; a structured input has no place to \
140	                 go on the wire to an agent",
141	                action.name, prompt.ty
142	            ),
143	            Some(directory) => format!(
144	                "`agent` action `{}` declares its prompt parameter `{}` as `{}` — with the \
145	                 working directory taken from `{directory}`, the parameter that remains is \
146	                 the `String` prompt handed to the harness; a structured input has no place \
147	                 to go on the wire to an agent",
148	                action.name, prompt.name, prompt.ty
149	            ),
150	        };
151	        ctx.error(marker, message);
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	/// Whether a resolved type is the builtin `String`.
156	///
157	/// Deliberately NOT tolerant of `String?`: an optional prompt is a prompt that
158	/// may be absent, and an absent prompt is not a call an agent can serve.
159	/// [`Ty::Unknown`] passes so a type that already failed to resolve reports once,
160	/// at its own site, rather than a second time as a shape complaint here.
161	fn is_string(ty: &Ty) -> bool {
162	    matches!(ty, Ty::Str | Ty::Unknown)
163	}
164	
165	/// Whether the declared return type is (structurally) the canonical
166	/// agent-outcome record: exactly the three fields `text: String`,
167	/// `stop_reason: String`, and `session_id: String`, in any order, under any
168	/// declared name.
169	///
170	/// The check is structural through the type table — a `Named` reference
171	/// resolves to its definition, and each field's own type resolves too, so a
172	/// projected schema record of the same shape satisfies it exactly as a
173	/// declared shorthand record does. [`Ty::Unknown`] passes so a return type
174	/// that already failed to resolve reports once, at its own site.
175	fn returns_agent_outcome_record(returns: &Ty, table: &TypeTable) -> bool {
176	    match resolve(returns, table) {
177	        Ty::Unknown => true,
178	        Ty::Record(record) => {
179	            record.fields.len() == 3
180	                && field_is_string(&record, "text", table)
181	                && field_is_string(&record, "stop_reason", table)
182	                && field_is_string(&record, "session_id", table)
183	        }
184	        _ => false,
185	    }
186	}
187	
188	/// Whether `record` carries a field `name` whose type resolves to `String`.
189	///
190	/// `String?` is deliberately refused: both record fields are always present
191	/// on the wire — an empty reply is the honest empty string, never an absent
192	/// field — so an optional field would declare an absence that cannot happen.
193	fn field_is_string(record: &RecordTy, name: &str, table: &TypeTable) -> bool {
194	    record
195	        .field(name)
196	        .is_some_and(|field| matches!(resolve(&field.ty, table), Ty::Str | Ty::Unknown))
197	}

"task": "Detect and report pre-existing resource collisions in the stacked-dev worker's provision_workspace handler before provisioning begins, so that operators and dispatching agents see upfront what artifacts from previous runs are present \u2014 the detection is informational and does not change provisioning behavior. Because handlers.rs already exceeds 500 LOC (625 lines excluding blanks/comments, no test module), the collision detection logic SHALL live in a new .meridian/workflows/stacked-dev/worker/src/collision.rs module, called from provision_workspace in handlers.rs. Three read-only checks, one report: at the start of provision_workspace before the existing resolve_branch_name call, invoke the collision detection function with the brief_id, repo_root, and placement/isolation context to perform: (a) branch collision \u2014 test whether the candidate branch name stacked-dev-{brief_id} already exists in the repository by running git branch --list (or the equivalent yg branch existence check that try_branch_add uses internally); (b) norn session collision \u2014 test whether a session file exists at ~/.norn/sessions/{session_id} where session_id is the candidate branch name stacked-dev-{brief_id} (matching the worker's session-id derivation from workspace.branch); (c) worktree collision \u2014 test whether the expected worktree directory already exists on disk at the path provision_worktree would create ({repo_root}/.yggdrasil-worktrees/stacked-dev-{brief_id} for Worktree isolation) or the path provision_clone would create (/tmp/stacked-dev-clones/stacked-dev-{brief_id} for Remote placement). If one or more collisions are detected, emit a single warn-level tracing call carrying the brief_id and, for each collision type, whether it was found and the specific name or path that collides. If no collisions are detected, emit nothing \u2014 silence means a clean workspace. The detection is purely informational: it does not abort provisioning, does not remove stale artifacts, and does not alter the return value or error handling of provision_workspace. The existing collision handling (attempt-N branch suffixing in resolve_branch_name, rm -rf in provision_clone) continues to operate unchanged. Scope boundary \u2014 in: the collision detection function in collision.rs, the call site in provision_workspace, the structured warn-level report log, and tests asserting them. Out: changes to resolve_branch_name, provision_worktree, provision_clone, or the norn session management; automatic cleanup or removal of stale artifacts; any change to the provision_workspace return value, error type, or control flow.",

THE SYSTEM SHALL perform these checks as read-only operations: no branch is created or deleted, no session file is created or removed, no directory is created or removed. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT fail or return early based on the detection results \u2014 the checks are diagnostic and control flow proceeds to resolve_branch_name regardless of findings.",

"spec": "In src/stacked_dev/locals.gleam, mirroring the live-proven dev pattern invocation-for-invocation. WHEN locals.scout runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL invoke norn with argv [\"--print\", \"--session-id\", workspace.branch <> \"-scout\", \"--workspace-root\", workspace.path, \"--output-schema\", scout_output_schema(), \"--output-format\", \"json\", prompt] in workspace.path. WHEN locals.dev_review runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL invoke norn identically with session id workspace.branch <> \"-review\" and review_output_schema(). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT derive the scout or review session id from anything but the branch plus its stage suffix, and SHALL NOT reuse the bare dev session id ('<branch>') for either stage (CN4, S9, S11). locals.dev SHALL use input.prompt as the positional prompt (its internal dev_prompt assembly and the old DevResult output schema are deleted) and keep session id = workspace.branch (C12); locals.dev_resume SHALL keep [\"--print\", \"--resume\", session_id, ...] and both SHALL pass dev_output_schema(), now the dev-report shape. Output parsing for all four norn-backed locals SHALL accept the bare report shape or the real {\"output\": ...} envelope only, and SHALL NOT accept any other wrapper; a norn invocation that cannot run or exits non-zero is a Terminal activity failure carrying diagnostics (CN5 \u2014 never a silent skip). The three schema-text constants (scout_output_schema, dev_output_schema, review_output_schema) are Gleam string constants; create test/stage_schema_test.gleam asserting each parses as JSON and is structurally equal (Erlang term equality of parsed Dynamics) to schemas/scout_report.json, schemas/dev_report.json, and schemas/review_report.json read from the package root \u2014 pinning the inline constants to the drift-gated package schemas.",

"spec": "Create src/brief_dev.gleam (deleting src/onatopp_dev.gleam \u2014 brief_dev takes its slot, ADR-008) with pub const workflow_type = \"brief_dev\", pub const status_query_name = \"brief_dev_status\", definition() binding the R2 codecs to execute, and run() mirroring the existing raw-input entry convention. Flow: WHEN execution starts, THE SYSTEM SHALL register status (\"scouting\", 0) and run the scout activity with prompts.scout_prompt(document, context); IF scout fails, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail with ScoutFailed (C11). WHEN scout succeeds, THE SYSTEM SHALL register (\"developing\", 0) and dispatch workflow.all([activities.warm_build(workspace), activities.dev(DevInput(workspace, prompts.dev_prompt(document, context, scout_report)))]) \u2014 the tagged StartupTask fan-out preserved, results in input order, a shape violation failing as BriefDevStageFailed(stage: \"startup\") (C12). IF the dev report contains any enrichment with status blocked, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail with DevBlocked listing those R# ids (C18). WHILE verifying, THE SYSTEM SHALL register (\"verifying\", round) and run scoped_checks over the deduplicated files_changed paths of the latest dev report; on CheckPass proceed to review; on CheckFail, IF round >= verify_fix_cap THEN fail with VerifyFixExhausted(rounds, diagnostics), ELSE register (\"fixing\", round), durably sleep round_backoff_ms, run dev_resume(ResumeInput(session_id: workspace.branch, feedback: prompts.resume_feedback(document, diagnostics))) for a full replacement DevReport, and recurse with round + 1 (C13 \u2014 onatopp semantics preserved, both bounds are required inputs, no default anywhere, ADR-001/ADR-003). WHEN verification converges, THE SYSTEM SHALL register (\"reviewing\", round) and run dev_review with prompts.review_prompt(document, context, scout_report, latest_dev_report, converged_check_result) \u2014 the reviewer sees the attestation AND the measured result (S10) in its own session (C14). IF any review enrichment has alignment drifted, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail with ReviewDrifted carrying every drifted enrichment's id and issues (C16). IF any review enrichment's fixes list is non-empty, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL register (\"hardening\", round) and re-run scoped_checks with the same files_touched; IF that re-run fails, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail with HardenRegressed(diagnostics) (C15). WHEN converged, THE SYSTEM SHALL register (\"converged\", round) and return BriefDevResult(scout, final dev report, review report, verify_rounds, build_warm). The status handler is re-registered at every transition with exactly the phases scouting, developing, verifying, fixing, reviewing, hardening, converged (C17, S6). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT read the filesystem, write the brief file, or call any enrichment (CN1/P5 \u2014 BD-004 inserts enrich_brief call sites later), SHALL NOT impose any cap, backoff, or deadline beyond the two required inputs, and SHALL NOT dispatch any activity other than scout, warm_build, dev, scoped_checks, dev_resume, and dev_review. LOC note: the module is estimated above 300 lines; its behavioural tests live in BD-007's hermetic suite by design, and its codec tests in R7 \u2014 no test code in this module.",

An empty list is the honest answer for a workflow with no live agent attempt, not an error. |

| `POST` | `/workflows/transcript` | Read the retained agent-observability transcript tail of one `(workflow, activity, attempt)` stream from `from_seq` (default 0), in `store_seq` order. An unknown or pre-retention stream returns `200` with empty `events`, null `next_from_seq`, and `head_seq == 0`. |

The `transcript` arm streams the agent-observability transcript of one `(workflow, activity, attempt)` — two attempts of one activity are distinct streams. It is namespace-scoped exactly like `per_workflow` (authorized by the caller's namespace grant, never the deploy grant). Optional `after_seq` is the highest `store_seq` the client has already applied: the server replays the durable transcript tail with `store_seq > after_seq`, then splices onto the live broadcast with no gap and no duplicate. Absent `after_seq` = a fresh subscriber that must see the full durable transcript from `store_seq == 0`. `POST /workflows/transcript` is the request/response counterpart over plain HTTP.

196	### Agent seams
197	
198	`agent` says exactly one thing: the action's single `String` parameter carries
199	a PROMPT and its result is the canonical agent-outcome record — a record you
200	declare yourself, under any name, with exactly three fields: `text: String`
201	(the agent's terminal reply), `stop_reason: String` (the canonical snake_case
202	stop reason: `end_turn | tool_use | limit_reached | cancelled | error |
203	other`), and `session_id: String` (the handle of the conversation that
204	produced the outcome — a fact the harness fills, not a promise the session
205	can be resumed; it is meaningful only to the harness that minted it). That is
206	the whole of what an adapter needs to hand the call to an
207	agent harness instead of running it as an ordinary activity, and it is the
208	shape every harness emits: each maps its native terminal outcome onto the
209	record at its own boundary, so the flow reads `reply.text` — and can route on
210	`reply.stop_reason` — without ever parsing harness-specific JSON.
211	
212	```awl
213	//! Ask an agent one question and route its reply text.
214	workflow ask_the_agent
215	  input question: String
216	  outcome done: type String, route success
217

200	declare yourself, under any name, with exactly three fields: `text: String`

12	//// conversation that produced the outcome. The handle is a fact, not a
13	//// promise: it names the session the harness actually ran and says nothing
14	//// about whether it can be resumed (resumability is the harness's own

16	//// resume routing pairs it with the harness identity the workflow record
17	//// already carries.

1	//// Pins the Gleam-side canonical agent-outcome record (`aion/agent`) to the
2	//// exact wire shape the Rust harnesses emit from `wait_result` — a JSON
3	//// object of `text` + `stop_reason` + `session_id`, snake_case, nothing
4	//// else. The decode side is exercised against harness-authored bytes (key
5	//// order the Rust serializer produces) rather than only against this codec's
6	//// own encode, so the pin cannot degenerate into a self-consistency check.
7	
8	import aion/agent.{AgentOutcome}
9	import gleam/string
10	import gleeunit/should
11	
12	pub fn the_record_round_trips_through_its_codec_test() {
13	  let codec = agent.outcome_codec()
14	  let outcome =
15	    AgentOutcome(
16	      text: "the answer",
17	      stop_reason: "end_turn",
18	      session_id: "sess-roundtrip",
19	    )
20	  let wire = codec.encode(outcome)
21	  codec.decode(wire)
22	  |> should.equal(Ok(outcome))
23	}
24	
25	pub fn the_harness_wire_bytes_decode_test() {
26	  // Bytes as the Rust side writes them (serde field order: text first).
27	  let codec = agent.outcome_codec()
28	  codec.decode(
29	    "{\"text\":\"done\",\"stop_reason\":\"end_turn\",\"session_id\":\"sess-wire-9\"}",
30	  )
31	  |> should.equal(
32	    Ok(AgentOutcome(
33	      text: "done",
34	      stop_reason: "end_turn",
35	      session_id: "sess-wire-9",
36	    )),
37	  )
38	}
39	
40	pub fn an_empty_text_on_a_completed_run_is_honest_test() {
41	  let codec = agent.outcome_codec()
42	  codec.decode(
43	    "{\"text\":\"\",\"stop_reason\":\"end_turn\",\"session_id\":\"sess-quiet\"}",
44	  )
45	  |> should.equal(
46	    Ok(AgentOutcome(text: "", stop_reason: "end_turn", session_id: "sess-quiet")),
47	  )
48	}
49	
50	pub fn a_bare_string_is_refused_by_the_decoder_test() {
51	  // The pre-#181 wire shape must not decode: the record is the contract now.
52	  let codec = agent.outcome_codec()
53	  let assert Error(failure) = codec.decode("\"just text\"")
54	  failure.reason
55	  |> string.is_empty
56	  |> should.be_false
57	}
58	
59	pub fn a_two_field_payload_is_refused_by_the_decoder_test() {
60	  // The pre-#205 wire shape must not decode either: `session_id` is a
61	  // mandatory fact, and a payload without it is a stale producer, not a
62	  // record to accept quietly.
63	  let codec = agent.outcome_codec()
64	  let assert Error(failure) =
65	    codec.decode("{\"text\":\"done\",\"stop_reason\":\"end_turn\"}")
66	  failure.reason
67	  |> string.is_empty
68	  |> should.be_false
69	}

15	  `cargo build` ships the real UI.
16	
17	### Embed pipeline
18	
19	The ops console is part of the product: `crates/aion-server/ops-console-embed/` is
20	a **committed** bundle and every build embeds it. You only run the pipeline to
21	**refresh** that committed bundle after changing the ops-console source:
22	
23	```sh
24	cargo xtask build-ops-console
25	```
26	
27	In order it: (a) regenerates the ts-rs wire types
28	(`cargo test -p aion-core export_ops_console_wire_types`), (b) runs
29	`bun install && bun run build` here, and (c) syncs `dist/*` into
30	`crates/aion-server/ops-console-embed/`. **Commit the refreshed bundle.**
31	
32	Then any build ships it — no feature flag:
33	
34	```sh
35	cargo build -p aion-cli --release
36	./target/release/aion server --open   # serves the ops console at the HTTP port
37	```
38	
39	**The bundle is committed.** `crates/aion-server/ops-console-embed/` holds the real
40	built `index.html`, `assets/**`, and `favicon.svg`. `rust_embed` reads it from
41	disk in debug builds and embeds it in release builds. The Vite config builds with
42	`sourcemap: false`, and the embed dir's `.gitignore` ignores stray `*.map` files.
43	
44	### CI guards (`.github/workflows/ops-console-embed.yml`)
45	
46	Two distinct guards (kept separate so there is no write-then-assert
47	contradiction):
48	
49	1. **wire-types-no-diff** — regenerate the ts-rs types and assert the committed
50	   generated files have no git diff (read-only assertion).
51	2. **embed-freshness** — `cargo xtask verify-ops-console` rebuilds the ops console
52	   into a scratch dir and diffs it against the committed `ops-console-embed/`
53	   bundle, failing if it is stale. It then builds a plain (no-feature) binary and
54	   `ci/smoke-embed.sh` runs it, failing if `/` does not serve the real UI.
55

57	
58	Wire types under `src/types/generated/` are generated from Rust-owned Aion types with the

60	The generated barrel carries a `@generated` header so review can distinguish wire output from local

56	## Generated wire types
57	
58	Wire types under `src/types/generated/` are generated from Rust-owned Aion types with the
59	house generated-types pipeline (`#[derive(TS)]` via `ts-rs`). Do not edit generated files by hand.
60	The generated barrel carries a `@generated` header so review can distinguish wire output from local
61	view models.
62	
63	Regenerate after changing exported Aion wire shapes:
64	
65	```sh
66	AION_UPDATE_BINDINGS=1 cargo test -p aion-core export_ops_console_wire_types
67	```
68	
69	**The environment variable is required, and the same command without it does the opposite.**
70	That test is the drift gate: by default it regenerates in memory, compares against the committed
71	file, and FAILS WITHOUT WRITING when they differ. It writes only under `AION_UPDATE_BINDINGS`.
72	
73	It works that way because it used to write unconditionally and assert nothing, so an ordinary
74	`cargo test` mutated a tracked file behind the developer's back — and the committed bindings could
75	be arbitrarily wrong while the whole Rust battery was green. They were.
76	
77	`cargo xtask build-ops-console` is the other sanctioned regeneration path and sets the variable
78	itself.
79	
80	The generation target for this app is `apps/aion-ops-console/src/types/generated/`. The public
81	`src/types/index.ts` file is only a barrel over generated wire types; local UI-only models belong in
82	feature-folder `types.ts` files.

1	# Agent workers
2	
3	How agent-backed activities get served in Aion. An **agent action** is an
4	activity whose work is done by an AI agent — its output is decided by the
5	agent at run time, so there is no Rust type to derive a schema from and the
6	AWL document is the only authority on what the action looks like. Its result
7	is always the **canonical agent-outcome record** — a declared record of
8	exactly `text: String` (the agent's terminal reply), `stop_reason: String`
9	(the canonical snake_case reason: `end_turn | tool_use | limit_reached |
10	cancelled | error | other`), and `session_id: String` (the handle of the
11	conversation that produced the outcome — a fact the harness fills, meaningful
12	only to the harness that minted it) — which every harness emits from its own
13	integration boundary, so a flow reads `reply.text` and never parses
14	harness-specific JSON. This guide covers the two ways to serve one:
15	
16	1. **`aion worker agent <file.awl>`** — the built-in agent worker. No crate
17	   to write: the binary you already installed serves the document's agent
18	   actions through a compiled-in harness (`norn` or `acp`).
19	2. **The assistant's example worker** (`examples/agent-dev/worker/`) — a
20	   hand-written Rust worker driving norn, kept as the reference for what a
21	   custom agent worker looks like and as the thing `scripts/setup.sh` runs.
22	
23	Related reading: [DECLARED-COMMANDS.md](DECLARED-COMMANDS.md) (an action
24	WITH a `run` body in the document is executed by the *server* — no worker of
25	any kind serves it, there is no sandbox, and that document is the whole
26	account of what is and is not guaranteed), and
27	[WORKER-AUTHORING.md](WORKER-AUTHORING.md) (ordinary Rust activity workers).
